subject: Quanton.ai - SLO/throughput validation & pilot plan
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@quanton.ai>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 16:23:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo: performance targets + next steps

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — the demo was really helpful. I wanted to summarize Quanton's performance targets and confirm next steps so we're aligned for a short pilot. Key constraints from our product team: 

- Key SLOs (initial):
  - P95 response time <= 250 ms for simple text completions (<= 128 tokens).
  - Streaming latency (first token) <= 80 ms for chat interactions.
  - Sustained throughput target: 200 concurrent chat sessions (avg 1 request/10s), peak bursts up to ~600 rps across burst windows.
  - Concurrency: We need support for 300 concurrent sessions with active KV caches.

- Workload shape: mostly short turn-taking chat (avg 40 tokens), occasional long generations up to 800 tokens for batch jobs.
- Security/ops: must run in Dedicated mode (tenant isolation) and preserve KV cache across sessions.

Can the team sketch a recommended GPU shortlist and a provisional reserved-throughput sizing for a pilot (2-week smoke) that demonstrates we can meet P95 and streaming targets? Also please note we attached recent sample traces and our SLO matrix (see attachments).

We'll loop in our infra lead if you need specific network/firewall details. Goal is to decide pilot size and schedule by EOW.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform, Quanton.ai

Attachments: quanton_sample_traces.csv, quanton_slo_matrix.xlsx
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@quanton.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance targets + next steps

Elena — great to get these specifics, thanks for the clear SLOs. Quick recap of what we'll do and an initial recommendation so your team can decide: 

Summary of ask (we heard):
- P95 <= 250 ms for short completions (<=128 tokens)
- First-token streaming <= 80 ms
- Sustained ~200 concurrent chat sessions, peak up to ~600 rps
- Must run on Dedicated capacity with KV/prefix caching preserved per session

Initial GPU shortlist & rationale (pilot-focused):
- H100 80GB (float + quantized): best single-GPU throughput and headroom for KV caching; expect strongest P95 under tight-latency SLOs for short sequences. Good for streaming at low token-latency.
- A10G / A30 class (24–40GB): cost-effective mid-range; better cost/throughput for batch workloads but likely needs more instances to hit P95 under bursty, low-latency chat.
- L4 (24GB) / inference-optimized accelerators: attractive price for cheaper models or heavy quantized configs; may struggle to meet strict P95 for chat streaming without more aggressive batching.

Provisional sizing (pilot, 2 weeks):
- Pilot target: validate P95 and streaming on production-like traces at ~200 concurrent sessions and burst windows up to 600 rps.
- Suggested starting pool: 3 x H100 (80GB) reserved GPUs. Rationale: gives headroom for KV cache and model variants, and simplified routing for latency-critical traffic. If we see comfortable P95 and low GPU utilization, we can re-size down or try mixed pools (H100 + A10 fleet) to reduce cost.
- Fallback plan: if cost is a concern, run a mixed pool: 2x H100 + 4x A10G and route warm sessions to A10G where possible.

Benchmark matrix we'll run during pilot (we'll deliver results):
- P95 latency and P99 for short (<=128) / medium (256–512) / long (512–800) tokens
- First-token streaming latency under different concurrency levels (50 / 200 / 300 concurrent)
- Tail latency under burst (600 rps sustained for 30s)
- Token throughput and GPU utilization per model variant and quantization (FP16, INT8, 4-bit)
- KV cache hit/miss impact on end-to-end latency

Next steps & timeline:
1) We'll provision a pilot cluster (Dedicated) with the 3x H100 config and run your sample traces in our perf lab. ETA to have results: 6 business days after we get access to full traces and any ACL/firewall details.
2) We'll share a short perf plan PDF and a runbook (attached: redwood_perf_plan.pdf).
3) After initial run, we’ll propose a reduced/mixed pool and a cost/latency tradeoff summary.

Ask from you: share a short-lived service account or test keys and confirm any egress restrictions. Also confirm whether KV caches must persist across restarts or only per-session.

I'll coordinate with Ben and Monica on ops and billing side — Ben will follow up on pilot contract and provisional commitment.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_perf_plan.pdf
From: Elena Morales <elena@quanton.ai>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 10:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance targets + next steps

Thanks Jasmine — this looks good and reasonable. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KV cache: must persist per-session for the duration of a user chat (session TTL = 24 hours). Persistence across host restarts is not required initially.
- Network: we'll whitelist Redwood pilot IPs and provide a test service account.
- We attached a small set of traces (sample long and short sessions) — please prioritize short-session latency tests.

We agree to the 3x H100 pilot to establish baseline performance. On procurement, we prefer a short, limited commitment for the pilot (2 weeks, no long-term financial commitment). After pilot results we'll decide on reserved capacity.

Can you confirm the earliest start date and share the perf runbook link?

-Elena

Attachments: quanton_sample_traces.csv, quanton_slo_matrix.xlsx
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: performance targets + next steps — pilot coordination

Forwarding Elena's confirmation. Action items for Redwood ops/sales to get pilot scheduled:

- Monica: please open a pilot ticket and reserve 3x H100 (Dedicated) for a 14-day window. Include a smoke-run slot (2 hours) and the full run (2 business days of sustained runs). Use PERF-742 as the internal reference.
- Jasmine: finish the perf plan (I reviewed redwood_perf_plan.pdf; add the exact commands we'll run and the trace subsets).
- Ben (me): I'll prepare a short pilot addendum (no financial commitment beyond the pilot) and share with Elena for signature. Include a narrow SLA for pilot availability only.
- Ops checklist: firewall IPs from Quanton (Elena will provide), service account creds, sample traces location (Drive link), and telemetry hook (trace logs + GPU metrics).

I'll cc legal if we need a one-off pilot addendum. Goal: pilot start as early as next week if infra access is ready.

Thanks — tagging PERF-742 on the ticket.

—Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
